scenario: An interrupted independent recruiter intentionally reviews one synthetic candidate-conversation capture, traces proposed facts and one action to exact evidence, checks a synthetic localhost session, explicitly approves Submit, and sees truthful loading, failure, unknown, retry, stale-session, receipt, and local-deletion states without any real external write.

review_plan.reason: The extension is responsive and must prove keyboard, assistive semantics, zoom, contrast, motion, and recovery.
The surface handles private candidate conversation evidence and must preserve dignity, restraint, and human control.
The core object is an intentional recruiter capture and review workflow.
Capture scope, provenance, authorization, idempotency, receipt truth, and deletion are release gates.
The artifact performs no candidate assessment or evaluator design; its deterministic blocked-inference fixture is a product boundary, not an assessment claim.

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The loaded package completes by keyboard with an ordered focus trace, 3px visible focus, four ARIA-live transitions, an inspectable Chromium accessibility tree, and zero reviewed axe violations or incomplete checks; however, the transcript is generated from the accessibility tree and not spoken output from a screen reader or an assistive-technology user.
findings.user_impact: The semantic path is directly inspectable and no automated blocker remains, but wording, verbosity, or announcement timing may still be confusing in an actual screen reader.
findings.recommendation: Run one user-visible Google Chrome traversal with a supported screen reader through evidence, session, approval, pending, failure, retry, and receipt.
findings.verification: The spoken order names the exact evidence before Submit, announces approval without implying submission, announces unknown without success, and completes without duplicate or ambiguous speech.

findings.observation: Persistent Chromium directly loaded the unpacked build and exercised 390, 320, actual tab zoom 2.0 to 195 CSS pixels, and a 195 CSS-pixel equivalent reflow with zero root overflow or clipped DOM elements; the page was opened as an extension tab because headless automation cannot prove the user's toolbar-opened Google Chrome side-panel container.
findings.user_impact: Reflow behavior is proven at the relevant CSS widths, while browser-owned panel resizing, pinning, and toolbar transition remain unobserved.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the same keyboard and 200% zoom path in a policy-authorized, user-visible Google Chrome side panel without changing the frozen package.
findings.verification: The browser-owned side panel preserves the same semantic order, visible focus, complete text, and reachable Submit at 320, 390, and 200% zoom.

strengths: The keyboard path reaches New capture, Remove, five exact-evidence controls, session check, retention, approval, and Submit in DOM order; every recorded keyboard focus has a 3px solid outline.

The actual Chromium tab reports zoom 2.0 and inner width 195 from a 390 CSS-pixel viewport; scroll width equals client width, the clipped-element audit is empty, and the equivalent reflow screenshot keeps long Latin, Chinese, and Arabic content readable.

Loading, no-action, ambiguity, blocked inference, permission denial, offline, retry, unknown, reconciliation, stale session, recovered receipt, and local deletion remain textually distinct without color-only meaning.
Dark increased-contrast reduced-motion output has transition duration 0s, transition property none, animation name none, and zero axe violations or incomplete checks.
missing_evidence: Spoken screen-reader output or assistive-technology user evidence.
User-visible Google Chrome side-panel container, toolbar transition, and browser-owned zoom observation.
open_questions: Does the evidence-link repetition remain efficient with a screen reader when several assertions cite the same message?

reviews.lens: human connection, trust, agency, communication, collaboration

findings.observation: The loaded package says it collects only visible pixels or an explicit selection, keeps exact evidence reviewable, supports Remove and minimization, stays silent on capture API handoff before explicit Submit, and labels all exercised content synthetic; the harness still cannot show the user's Google Chrome toolbar gesture and positive temporary activeTab grant.
findings.user_impact: The review surface treats candidate conversation evidence with restraint, but a live recruiter cannot yet rely on this run to prove that real evidence enters only through the promised visible gesture.
findings.recommendation: Record one policy-authorized Google Chrome toolbar or shortcut capture of synthetic conversation content, keeping the exact selected asset visible until explicit Submit.
findings.verification: The recording shows the gesture, temporary source scope, exact review, optional minimization or removal, no capture handoff before Submit, and no action beyond one localhost capture receipt.

findings.observation: The UI explains three requested retention modes and explicitly says a receipt does not prove deletion; after the synthetic text receipt it distinguishes Deleted locally from unverified backend derivative deletion. No candidate-facing notice, recruiter agreement, or backend retention/deletion behavior is part of the frozen artifact.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/18-local-deleted-backend-unverified-390.png; docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/review-object.json boundary and environment; apps/browser-extension/README.md Honest development limits
findings.user_impact: The interface avoids a deceptive deletion promise, while a live deployment would still need a humane, comprehensible explanation of why conversation evidence is captured and how long every derivative persists.
findings.recommendation: Before real candidate data, pair the extension with reviewed notice, purpose, retention, deletion, and recruiter-responsibility language tied to implemented backend controls.
findings.verification: A recruiter can accurately explain the purpose and lifecycle before importing real evidence, and source plus registered derivatives follow the selected policy in backend readback.

strengths: The blocked fixture says candidate scoring or ranking is outside the product boundary; no candidate worth, fit, personality, tone, protected trait, or acceptance probability is displayed.
The no-action fixture states that insufficient evidence creates no task, avoiding manufactured urgency or pressure on the candidate.
Every proposed fact and the single bounded question remain tied to exact observed words, while the UI repeatedly says the fixture is proposed and never confirmed candidate state.
The extension makes no contact, calendar, ATS, message, or other external write and describes the Submit effect as one capture handoff only.
Permission denial, offline, unknown, stale session, retry, receipt, Remove, and local deletion use candid language about what happened and what remains safe.
missing_evidence: User-visible Google Chrome gesture and positive temporary source grant.
Candidate-facing notice or consent-policy evaluation for real private conversation evidence.
Implemented backend retention and derivative deletion.
open_questions: What notice and accountability language will accompany the first use of real candidate conversation evidence?

findings.observation: The loaded package presents one three-step review order, keeps source and exact evidence visible, completes by keyboard, and recovers offline, unknown, and stale-session states without losing the reviewed packet; no uncoached recruiter completed the flow or compared it with copying a note manually.
findings.user_impact: The workflow is directly executable and recovery is inspectable, but this evidence cannot establish that a busy recruiter understands the distinctions quickly enough or saves more reconstruction than the manual fallback.
findings.recommendation: Run an uncoached timed comparison with independent recruiters using one synthetic conversation: current manual note/copy workflow versus the frozen extension.
findings.verification: Participants complete the extension path without prompting, correctly explain evidence versus proposal versus Submit versus receipt, catch one seeded scope error, and show lower reconstruction or omission cost than the fallback.

findings.observation: The package directly proves permission denial and the complete review-to-synthetic-receipt path, but the automated extension page cannot invoke the user's Google Chrome toolbar or shortcut to observe the positive activeTab-to-review transition.
findings.user_impact: The review itself is low-friction, while the real entry cost, source-tab return behavior, and first focused control after browser invocation remain unknown.
findings.recommendation: Run the frozen package in a policy-authorized user-visible Google Chrome profile and record toolbar and selected-text entry through the same keyboard review.
findings.verification: The recruiter opens the correct current source with one explicit gesture, reaches the exact reviewed asset without context reconstruction, and can remove or submit it without hidden tab access.

strengths: One information order stays visible: inspect evidence, check local session, submit explicitly.
Each proposed TS-CORE-01 fact and the single action exposes a keyboard-reachable exact-message link; the direct trace moves focus to the observed candidate message.
No-action, ambiguity, supersession, and blocked inference are first-class outcomes rather than generic errors or manufactured work.
Offline retains the reviewed packet for the same-packet retry, unknown disables resubmit until receipt check, and stale session requires refresh before the idempotent retry.
Long mixed-script content remains complete at 320 and 390 CSS pixels and reflows at the 195 CSS-pixel layout created by 200% tab zoom.
missing_evidence: Uncoached recruiter comprehension and time-versus-manual evidence.
Positive toolbar or shortcut capture in the user's Google Chrome.
Real localhost session and destination receipt, day-later resume, and backend deletion readback.
open_questions: Would a recruiter prefer one message-level evidence link shared by four assertions, or are per-assertion links faster when correcting a seeded error?

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

findings.observation: The exact build loads as a Manifest V3 extension in persistent Chromium, exposes only activeTab, scripting, sidePanel, and loopback hosts, directly shows permission denial, keeps the capture API silent through the synthetic keyboard review until explicit Submit, and preserves the exact asset and provenance; the evidence was produced by opening the extension page directly and cannot show the user's Google Chrome chrome://extensions installation, toolbar or shortcut invocation, or positive temporary activeTab grant.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/verification-summary.json artifact.manifest and aggregate_sha256; docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/loaded-package-evidence.json service_worker, extension_id, evidence_trace, keyboard_only_flow.pre_submit_capture_api_silence, and caveat; docs/evaluations/round-2/browser-extension/04-permission-denied-390.png
findings.user_impact: Without the user-visible positive grant trace, this run cannot prove that real candidate conversation evidence enters only after the promised deliberate source-scoped gesture or that the complete real capture-to-Submit boundary is silent.
findings.recommendation: Load the same aggregate package in a policy-authorized user Google Chrome profile, invoke the toolbar or configured shortcut on a synthetic source, inspect the exact selected text or viewport, and record extension-originated network activity through one Submit receipt.
findings.verification: One recording and trace show the installed package digest, explicit toolbar or shortcut gesture, temporary source-only activeTab access, exact reviewed asset, no capture POST before Submit, one Submit, one account-scoped synthetic receipt, and no other tab, history, cookie, or external effect access.

strengths: The machine inventory keeps private source pixels/text, source metadata, recruiter edits, fixture proposals, retention request, session version, authorization, idempotency, and receipt outcome as distinct assets and states.
Each TS-CORE-01 proposed fact and action can focus the exact observed message; superseded state preserves before and proposed-after values rather than destructively overwriting.
Changing the draft, retention, or localhost target invalidates approval and request identity; stale session blocks retry until refresh.
Pending, received, duplicate, failed, unknown, and stale remain distinct; unknown blocks resubmit and receipt check reconciles without a second Submit.
The offline retry reuses one request identity, the fixture duplicate path returns one receipt, and 31 deterministic tests plus integrated package tests pass.
A received synthetic selected-text sample clears private text locally while the UI separately states that backend retention and derivative deletion remain unverified.
The blocked fixture refuses candidate scoring and ranking, and the manifest contains no ambient collection, cookie, history, broad host, remote-code, or external-write surface.
missing_evidence: User Google Chrome chrome://extensions load and installed-package identity.
Positive toolbar or shortcut activeTab grant on a synthetic source.
Real-extension source-to-preview and pre-Submit network trace in user Google Chrome.
Real localhost browser-managed session, capture receipt, duplicate readback, retention, and derived deletion.
vetoes: XS-CAPTURE-01: the user Google Chrome intentional capture and pre-Submit source boundary remains unproven.

top_findings.reason: The exact package is directly executable in Playwright Chromium, but no user Google Chrome chrome://extensions/toolbar trace proves the positive temporary activeTab grant and real source-to-Submit silence boundary.
top_findings.next_step: Run the same package digest in a policy-authorized user Google Chrome profile with a synthetic source, toolbar or shortcut gesture, network trace, and one localhost receipt.
top_findings.verification: The trace shows one explicit gesture, source-only temporary access, the exact reviewed asset, no capture POST before Submit, one scoped receipt, and no background tab, history, cookie, or external effect access.

top_findings.reason: Keyboard focus, AX tree, ARIA live regions, 200% reflow, contrast, reduced motion, and axe checks pass directly, but automated semantics do not prove spoken screen-reader timing or uncoached human understanding.
top_findings.next_step: Run one uncoached recruiter walkthrough and one supported screen-reader traversal on the frozen package.
top_findings.verification: Both users complete the path and correctly distinguish evidence, proposal, approval, pending or unknown, receipt, and local versus backend deletion without coaching.

top_findings.reason: The extension truthfully requests retention and clears private content locally after receipt, but the owning backend has not proven a real receipt, duplicate readback, retention, or source-plus-derivative deletion.
top_findings.next_step: Have the localhost backend owner run the frozen extension request through a scoped synthetic session and lifecycle trace.
top_findings.verification: One request ID resolves to one receipt, duplicate reconciliation, the chosen retention result, and observable raw plus registered-derivative deletion.

agreements: Observed source, exact reviewed asset, synthetic proposal, explicit Submit authority, receipt outcome, and deletion state remain distinct.
The extension does not confirm candidate facts or execute contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other external writes.
Candidate scoring, ranking, personality, tone, protected traits, culture fit, and acceptance probability remain outside the product boundary.
The keyboard-only synthetic path completes in logical order with visible focus, exact-message links, no capture API request before Submit, and truthful receipt language.
Loading, no-action, ambiguity, blocked inference, permission denial, offline, unknown, retry, stale session, recovery, and local deletion preserve the reviewed context without false success.
Long mixed-script content reflows at 320, 390, and the 195 CSS-pixel layout created by 200% tab zoom; reviewed axe output has zero violations and zero incomplete checks.
Playwright Chromium evidence improves direct package proof but is not user Google Chrome toolbar evidence and cannot resolve XS-CAPTURE-01.

veto_resolution.veto: XS-CAPTURE-01: the user Google Chrome intentional capture and pre-Submit source boundary remains unproven.

adjudication.rationale: Executable evidence materially improves the extension craft and establishes a trustworthy bounded synthetic review surface. Mobile UX, candidate experience, and recruiter workflow each pass with bounded changes at score 3 under their own rubrics. Evidence safety owns the intentional-capture jurisdiction and retains one blocker: the allowed Chromium load-unpacked harness cannot prove the user's Google Chrome installation, toolbar gesture, or positive activeTab grant. Scores are not averaged, so the active veto keeps the release gate blocked. Real backend receipt and deletion also remain external evidence gaps rather than extension success claims.

next_tests.pass_condition: XS-CAPTURE-01 resolves with no background access, no capture POST before Submit, one reviewed packet, and no external effect.

next_tests.test: Run an uncoached recruiter walkthrough and supported screen-reader traversal of the frozen package.
next_tests.evidence_required: Task recording, spoken order, comprehension account, seeded-scope-error correction, hesitations, and completion time versus manual copy or note.
next_tests.pass_condition: Users finish without coaching, catch the seeded scope error, and accurately explain evidence, proposal, approval, receipt, and deletion limits.

next_tests.test: Run one scoped synthetic extension receipt, duplicate, retention, and deletion lifecycle.
next_tests.evidence_required: Request ID, idempotency key, session version, receipt readback, duplicate reconciliation, selected retention, and source plus derivative deletion readback.
next_tests.pass_condition: Exactly one receipt exists and every registered private derivative follows the disclosed retention or deletion result.
